title: Staying healthy as a working drummer
summary: Prayer, good food, rest, little drinking; he suspects bronchitis and allergies.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: There was another topic that I wanted to ask you about. That is for drummers. Drummers exert themselves a great deal when they're playing, perhaps in a different way, more than other members of the band. How have you managed to take care of your health all these years?
I think I had something to do with it. I say my...

I say my prayers every night. And I eat good food -- my wife cooks for me. Good food. And I get plenty of rest when I'm not working. And the only time I drink a little bit is when I'm working, if it's at night. The nights I'm not working, I don't drink anything at all no more, except a cola, Coca-Cola or something. And I take a little brandy once in a while.

But right now... I keep on saying I'm going to the doctor; I haven't gone yet. I have an allergy which is, I can't stand anybody smoking around me. It gets down in my throat, and I cough. And I'm a little bit allergic to different flowers. Different things. And when they get out in the air... When I get in a really hot place, I have to have air. Otherwise, I have to... Well, it ain't for me to say. It's for the doctor to say. The next thing to asthma...what is that...? Bronchitis. I think I have that.
